title: Choose a data type
summary: A data type describes how values are stored. An explicit type avoids guessing when size or precision matters.
introduction: A data type describes how values are stored. An explicit type avoids guessing when size or precision matters. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A data type describes how values are stored. An explicit type avoids guessing when size or precision matters.

blocks.code:
import numpy as np

values = np.array([1, 2], dtype=np.float32)
print(values.dtype)
blocks.title: Choose a data type

blocks.text: The output is float32. The values are stored as 32-bit floating-point numbers.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Print values.tolist to see the decimal values.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Floating-point values cannot represent every decimal fraction exactly.
For more detail later, use this [NumPy further reading](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/user/absolute_beginners.html).
